chunks: And whatever is in it from Abu Thamamah, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil, and Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim - may Allah be pleased with them - from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Abu Thamamah, the companion of Abu Jafar Al-Thani, peace be upon him.

key_terms.أَبُو ثَمَامَةَ: Abu Thamamah, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ الثَّانِي: Abu Jafar Al-Thani, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (the 6th Imam)
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ مَاجِيلَوَيْهَ: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, a prominent Shia narrator

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator chain for Abu Thamamah's hadith in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq establishes the authenticity of the narration by citing his direct teachers—Majillawayh, Ibn al-Mutawakkil, and Ibn Ibrahīm—who transmitted from Ali ibn Ibrahīm al-Qummi, thereby linking the report to Abu Thamamah, a trusted companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS). This detailed isnad underscores the rigorous scholarly methodology employed in Shia hadith compilation to ensure the reliability of traditions derived from the Ahl al-Bayt.
